Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Conveyancing Paralegal role at Mallory Pryce. I am based in the Reading area and am looking to move into a property-focused paralegal position where I can apply my caseload management, drafting and client-care experience within a busy, client-focused team.

During my year-long placement at Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner, I spent six months in the Real Estate Disputes team supporting a varied caseload of landlord and tenant, leasehold, easement and rights-of-light matters. I prepared electronic hearing bundles, assisted with skeleton arguments and court materials, conducted legal and factual research, and maintained matter records through iManage across several simultaneous matters with competing deadlines. That experience gave me a solid grounding in property law concepts and in the disciplined file management and deadline tracking that a busy property team requires.

More broadly, I have worked with high document volumes in complex, deadline-sensitive environments throughout my career. At BCLP's International Arbitration team I became the sole junior on a significant matter shortly before a major procedural deadline — coordinating documents, tracking outstanding actions and helping ensure on-time submission. I am comfortable working at pace without letting accuracy or client care slip.

In my current role as a Legal Adviser at Citizens Advice East Berkshire I manage matters from initial client instruction through to submission: taking detailed factual statements, drafting correspondence, preparing document schedules and maintaining confidential case records. Communicating clearly with clients about procedural requirements — including clients who find legal processes unfamiliar or stressful — is a regular part of the role, and I take client care seriously.

I hold an LLB (2:1, UCL) and am completing an LLM in Comparative and International Dispute Resolution at Queen Mary. I am keen to consolidate my property law knowledge within a residential conveyancing practice and to contribute to the efficient workflows and excellent client service your team is known for.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Fernanda Silva

I am writing to apply for the Paralegal (Clinical Negligence) position at your Reading firm. My background in disputes, case management and client-facing legal work maps directly onto the responsibilities you have described, and I am keen to bring that experience to a clinical negligence caseload.

At Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner, I supported both international arbitration and real estate disputes across the full lifecycle of proceedings: reviewing and organising evidence, preparing hearing bundles, drafting procedural documents, tracking deadlines and coordinating with clients on outstanding matters. Shortly before a significant submission deadline I became the only junior supporting the arbitration team, taking responsibility for document coordination and ensuring on-time delivery — feedback from the partner and associate placed my performance at newly qualified solicitor level.

In my current role at Citizens Advice East Berkshire I manage matters independently from initial instruction through to submission. I interview clients on sensitive matters, take detailed factual statements, identify evidential gaps and draft correspondence and procedural applications — all while translating complex rules into clear, practical guidance for people in difficult circumstances. That combination of rigorous case preparation and considered client communication is, I understand, central to clinical negligence work, where clients are often vulnerable and the procedural stakes are high.

I am familiar with the discipline required to manage competing deadlines across a live caseload, maintain accurate and confidential case records, and draft documents to a standard that can go directly to partners and counsel. I am also comfortable working in an environment where attention to detail and sound judgement on priorities are non-negotiable.

Reading is my local area and I am available to start promptly. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your team.

Yours faithfully,
Maria Fernanda Silva
